Hi Sara / Tom — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

TL;DR (from your asks)
- Pilot: small dedicated pool for evaluation, must preserve latency under load and avoid "noisy neighbor" interference.
- Production target: preferrable move to Dedicated capacity or Private VPC depending on procurement timeframe and security checklist results.
- Compliance: need SOC2 evidence and network diagram for VPC peering/firewall setup.

Notes from the discovery:
- Workload: conversational routing for support use case, avg 45 requests/sec during peak, median request size ~350 tokens, some request bursts to ~120 rps for short windows.
- SLOs: Brightly wants p95 latency under 300ms for 256-token responses; p99 budget is looser but still important for UX.
- Data controls: logs retention policy, KMS key management, and ability to restrict model routing (no model spillover).
- Ops: team wants predictable billing for production and the ability to reserve capacity during seasonal spikes.

Redwood options (high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest to start, shared infra, standard tenancy. Good for initial experimentation but requires trust in our noisy-neighbor mitigations.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools for your org, configurable autoscaling/burst settings, stronger isolation and capacity guarantees.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full network isolation and customer-managed control plane; best for regulated or data-sensitive workloads.

Attachments: I attached a short deployment options sheet with capacity/latency tradeoffs and a checklist for the SOC2/network items you asked about (redwood-deployment-options-sheet.pdf).

Suggested next steps:
- Tech deep-dive with Aditya to validate SLOs and run a brief perf test (30–45m). (Action: Steph to schedule)
- Share SOC2 excerpt and network diagram (we can send a redacted version first). (Action: Aditya to share)
- Procurement touchpoint: Marissa will draft an initial estimate for Dedicated capacity to pilot for 3 months. (Action: Marissa)

Are you okay with that plan? If so I’ll get the tech session on the calendar for early next week.

Thanks —

Thanks Steph — appreciate the concise recap. A couple of clarifying questions from our infra/security and product team before the tech deep-dive: 

1) Isolation guarantees: when you say "Dedicated capacity", what isolation guarantees exist at the node level? If another tenant saturates their pool, can that impact our pre-provisioned capacity? We want to understand eviction/overcommit behavior.
2) Latency SLOs: can you share real-world p95/p99 numbers for models around the 350-token mark on Dedicated pools vs Hosted?
3) Burst behavior: we have short bursts up to ~120 rps — how does autoscaling/burst capacity work without violating latency SLOs and how quickly can you scale?
4) Networking: We will need a high-level network diagram for the VPC path and whether you support private peering (no public ingress). Also need to verify firewall/TLS termination points.
5) Compliance: SOC2 doc or redacted excerpt would be helpful for our audit team.

Our timeline: aiming to start a pilot in late Jan (internal approvals permitting). For the pilot we want predictable capacity and isolated performance to evaluate UX.

If Aditya can answer 1–3 in the thread that would help us prep for the deep-dive. Otherwise happy to take the call.

Hi Tom / Sara — copying Marissa and Steph. Quick answers inline and an ops-level description so your infra team can vet feasibility before the call.

1) Isolation guarantees (Dedicated capacity):
- Dedicated = reserved GPU pool partitioned at the tenant level. We pin your workloads to a set of worker nodes that are not shared for inference. That prevents cross-tenant scheduling for inference requests on those nodes.
- Eviction policy: Dedicated pools are not preemptible for inference; we only reclaim capacity if a customer explicitly reduces their reservation or in extreme maintenance events (with 72h notice for planned maintenance).
- For hosted (shared) nodes we rely on QoS scheduling and continuous batching; noisy neighbor effects are mitigated but not absolutely eliminated.

2) Latency SLOs (real-world reference):
- On Dedicated pools our internal benchmarks for medium-sized sequence workloads (~350 tokens) show p95 around 120–220ms depending on model family and tokenization, p99 typically under 450–600ms under steady-state.
- Hosted shared infra p95 is similar for modest loads but degrades more under noisy bursty tenants.
- We can run a short perf test using a narrow prompt set to validate for your model and target sequence length.

3) Burst & autoscaling behavior:
- Dedicated pools support two burst modes: (a) configured burst buffer (warm spare nodes reserved to absorb short spikes) and (b) transient burst-to-hosted-fallback (if you allow it) where extra traffic is routed to compatible hosted variants.
- Typical autoscale reaction is sub-30s for spin-up of additional worker containers within a pre-warmed node pool; full GPU node spin-up from zero can take minutes which is why we recommend warm spare nodes for predictable short bursts.

4) Networking & VPC peering:
- We support AWS PrivateLink and VPC Peering in major regions; we provide a reference network diagram (attached: redwood-network-diagram.pdf) showing peering points, NAT/egress points, and recommended firewall rules. TLS termination happens at the edge; you can restrict traffic to private endpoints for the Private offering.

5) Compliance / SOC2:
- Attached is a redacted SOC2 excerpt covering controls relevant to data access, separation, and logging (SOC2-excerpt.pdf). We can provide the full auditor report under NDA if required.

Other operational notes:
- Caching & KV-warmup: cold-cache latency can spike on first few requests; for production we recommend a short warmup phase and pre-warming KV caches for heavy conversational workloads.
- Model routing & rollbacks: we can pin you to specific model versions and have an automatic fallback policy (e.g., lighter quantized variants) to preserve latency SLOs if the primary variant falters.

Next steps suggested:
- Schedule 45m perf-deep-dive with your platform eng + Aditya + our infra ops to confirm concrete p95 targets and run a quick smoke perf test. (Action: Steph to schedule)
- Marissa to put together a 3-month Dedicated pilot estimate including warm-spare configuration and burst buffer pricing. (Action: Marissa)
- I’ll upload the detailed network diagram and a short note on recommended firewall rules to the shared Drive link.

Happy to expand on any of these points on the call.

Best —
